questions.question: Explain what institutional racism is and evaluate its usefulness.

points.text: Institutional racism: collective failure of an organisation due to race (Macpherson). Found in police, education, CJS. Useful: explains systemic patterns without individual racist intent. Criticism: can be too vague.

questions.question: Describe the evidence for ethnic inequality in employment and crime.

points.text: Employment: Wood's CV study proved discrimination (74% more callbacks for White names). Crime: Black people 9x more likely to be stopped; 12% of prison vs 3% of population. Causes: discrimination, institutional racism, socio-economic factors.

questions.question: Evaluate whether legislation has effectively reduced ethnic inequality.

points.text: Legislation has improved formal equality but discrimination persists (CV studies, stop and search). Legislation addresses individual discrimination but not structural inequality. Conclusion: necessary but not sufficient.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Evaluate the view that institutional racism is the main cause of ethnic inequality in modern Britain. <div class="

points.text: A grade 9 response will: define institutional racism; present evidence (stop and search, CV studies); evaluate: it explains systemic patterns; counter-arguments: socio-economic factors also contribute; some ethnic groups achieve above average; conclude: institutional racism is significant but interacts with class and cultural factors. The most effective approach addresses all three.
